planRounds.resolution: Sent back to the architect, who revised the design to settle it.

conflicts.why: The design merges looks in an order where the variant look beats the size look, but R4 requires the size look to beat the variant look. A toggle with a variant and a size that set the same property would get the wrong value, and the R4 acceptance test could never pass as designed.
conflicts.evidence: R4 acceptance: 'the size look wins over the variant look, and the variant look wins over the all-toggles look' (fact: 'built-in look, all toggles, variant, size, per-button override', lowest to highest). Design summary: 'using the precedence all-toggles < size < variant < provider theme < per-button (R4, R5, R6)', which puts variant above size.

findings.description: Resource-fetching string forms get through the value filter. Only matters if style values ever come from untrusted input. Consider also rejecting image-set( and src( .
findings.evidence: FORBIDDEN_VALUE blocks url( but not CSS functions that take a quoted string and fetch it, e.g. background-image: image-set("https://host/x.png" 1x). Values stay confined to one property, so no rule, selector or script can be added.

findings.description: Check styleElement.isConnected before reuse and re-append when it is detached.
findings.evidence: styleElement is cached at module level. If something else removes it from document.head, styleElement stays non-null but detached, so later rules are appended to a detached element and never apply.

findings.description: Documentation should recommend a stable (module-level or memoised) style object for large lists.
findings.evidence: Compiles are memoised by object identity (WeakMap). A per-button inline toggleOptions.style, or an inline provider config, is a new object on each parent render and is recompiled and rehashed each time. The rule is still shared by id, so only CPU cost, not leaks.

findings.description: Configured looks are missing before hydration, so a toggle may briefly show the built-in look. This is a known trade-off of the design. Mention it in the docs.
findings.evidence: Rules are inserted in an effect only. In server-rendered HTML (Next.js) the button carries data-zest-toggle-style but no rule exists until hydration.

findings.description: Unrelated whitespace change on an existing line; the repo policy asks for minimal diffs. No behaviour change.
findings.evidence: The existing import line was edited as part of the diff: `from './ZestButton';// Assuming ...` lost the space before the trailing comment.

findings.description: Collision is very unlikely, but a longer hash or a body-keyed registry would remove the risk.
findings.evidence: The id is a 32-bit djb2 hash plus the length. Two different rule bodies could in theory map to the same id, and the second would then reuse the first one's rules.

findings.description: Stronger proof would be a test that the built-in toggle focus class or rule is present for on and off. The pre-existing toggle tests and the no-override assertion cover the main risk, so this is not blocking.
findings.evidence: The R7 test only asserts the generated sheet has no 'focus-visible' rule. Nothing asserts the built-in focus ring exists on the toggle in both off and on states (jsdom cannot compute CSS-module styles).

findings.description: Add a console.error/console.warn spy to one ignored-setting test. Behaviour is otherwise covered (null returned, button stays mounted).
findings.evidence: The R8 acceptance line 'No console error is produced for an ignored setting' has no console.error spy in any listed test. The hostile-config tests only check that nothing throws or unmounts.

findings.description: Consider an SSR test (renderToString with a styled provider, no document access during render) and a note that React 19 is covered only by the peer-dependency range. Advisory.
findings.evidence: The R9 edge case (React 18 and 19, Next.js App Router client components) has no test beyond the existing peer-dependency and build-externalization suites. The hook and sheet use no React 19-only API, but no test renders under both versions or checks SSR safety (document access at render).

findings.description: Ordering is a reasonable proxy and the integration test keeps the pressed state on a disabled toggle, so this is not blocking.
findings.evidence: The on+disabled edge case ('disabled look layered on the on look') is proven only by selector order (indexOf of the on rule is below the disabled rule). No test renders an on and disabled toggle and checks that both rules apply.

findings.description: Not provable in this project's setup, so it is recorded as advisory. Run a one-off gzip size comparison of dist before release. Also not run: the packed-library install and import under CommonJS and ES modules (no scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs).
findings.evidence: The NFR bundle-growth check (no more than 5 KB gzipped) and the check that the library's own CSS adds no new px sizes have no automated test. The project has no .size-limit.json and no size script. package.json dependencies are unchanged. The suite re-runs of R9 and R10 pass.

findings.description: A value can still make the browser request an external URL (tracking beacon) without writing url(). This does not add rules or scripts, so R-security (single property only) holds; the values come from the app developer, not end users. Consider also rejecting image-set(, image(, src(, cross-fade(, element( or documenting that values are trusted.
findings.evidence: FORBIDDEN_VALUE blocks url( but not other CSS functions that fetch resources from a string, e.g. image-set("https://host/x.png" 1x), cross-fade(), image(), src(). They contain no ; { } \ or url( so sanitizeValue accepts them for background-image, border-image, content, list-style-image, cursor.

findings.description: Unbounded input is a low-severity DoS/memory risk if a very large or dynamically generated style object is supplied. Consider a cap on properties per state, or document that the config must be static.
findings.evidence: collectStates iterates Object.keys(look) with no cap on the number of properties, and sizes/variants maps are unbounded; only each value is capped at 500 chars. The cache key includes the variant and size strings.

findings.description: Two different style bodies that collide would share the first one's CSS. This is a correctness risk rather than a vulnerability; accidental collision is unlikely and an attacker would already control the developer config. Consider keying the registry by the full css string, or comparing css on reuse.
findings.evidence: The rule id is a 32-bit djb2 hash plus text length, and toggleStyleSheet.acquireToggleStyle reuses the first entry registered for an id without comparing css.

findings.description: Under a strict CSP (style-src without 'unsafe-inline') the injected rules are blocked and toggles fall back to the library defaults. The library already injects CSS at runtime (rollup inject: true), so this is consistent with the existing behaviour. Worth a documentation note.
findings.evidence: The shared <style> element is created without a nonce.

findings.description: Each render of such a button recompiles its style and adds a throwaway cache entry (garbage-collected via WeakMap). The work is bounded by one button's style and does not leak, so this is only a note; the docs should recommend hoisting style objects.
findings.evidence: compileToggleStyle is memoised in a WeakMap keyed by the provider and per-button style objects. An inline zest.toggleOptions.style object is new on every render.
